## 固定收益市場主線

10月8日，美國長天期公債走揚。投資人在殖利率已升至高檔之際順利承接$220億30年期公債標售，隨後美國總統川普決定在期中選舉結束前暫緩進一步攻擊伊朗，又為市場帶來一些喘息。30年期殖利率下降7.02個基點至5.6001%，10年期下降5.69個基點至5.2268%。這波反彈使殖利率曲線趨平，實質殖利率與長期通膨補償均回落，但油價收盤仍大幅上漲。

買盤主要集中在近期賣壓已使絕對殖利率更具吸引力的年期，並未伴隨聯準會緊縮方向的轉變。Christopher Waller主張進一步升息，但時點可以彈性安排；Alberto Musalem則認為未來六至九個月仍需加強緊縮。最新勞動數據顯示裁員仍有限，房貸利率上升則說明借款人已承受更大的壓力。

公司信用市場的復甦並不一致。科技公司的融資需求持續擴張，推升違約保險成本至紀錄高點，儘管較廣泛的股票市場大致抵擋了科技股下跌的衝擊。歐洲方面，法國企業融資成本低於政府的新證據，凸顯跨國企業獲利與主權財政風險的分野。各國央行仍表示通膨的第二輪效應有限，但政府與脆弱借款人的選擇正變得愈來愈昂貴。

## 長債買盤抵銷盤初能源壓力

能源疑慮再起，盤初曾推高美債殖利率，隨後30年期標售為市場帶來明確的長天期債券需求。這筆$220億標售以5.618%得標，接近紐約下午1時投標截止時的發行前交易殖利率5.617%。一級交易商承接比例僅6.8%，低於近期平均的10%，留給中介機構吸收的份額格外小。前一次30年期標售的得標殖利率為5.308%；此次政府付出的融資成本明顯更高，需求仍穩健。

星期四最長年期的新券再度順利被市場吸收，殖利率也進一步下降，延續本週長債承接良好的表現。財政部其後買回$60億、剩餘期限介於20至30年的公債，這是擴大買回計畫以來第四次此類操作。在投資人消化新券後，買回又為流通中的長債帶來另一筆需求。

TD Securities利率策略師Molly Brooks認為，標售需求顯示較高殖利率開始吸引買家；若價格能守住漲幅、漲勢維持數日，可能促使一直等待市場更穩定的投資人進場。

川普的社群媒體聲明讓漲勢延伸。他表示，美國不會在11月3日期中選舉前再次攻擊伊朗，並稱與德黑蘭的討論富有成效，但未說明細節。稍早《大西洋》報導白宮已要求五角大廈準備選前攻擊方案，這項聲明扭轉了市場對近期行動的預期。RBC Capital Markets策略師Izaac Brook將油價與長天期殖利率的部分回落，歸因於短期衝突升級風險解除。

實體供應仍然吃緊。油輪再遭攻擊，威脅荷姆茲海峽近期改善的運輸流量；颶風Isaias也使美國墨西哥灣業者關閉油井、撤離人員。布蘭特原油盤中一度在每桶$105附近交易，之後回落，但在固定收益市場收盤時仍為$103.79，上漲3.58%；WTI為$91.11，上漲3.21%。外交消息雖使行情離開當日極端價位，能源價格仍明顯高於前收。

航運情況也顯示干擾可能延長。超大型油輪為爭取高運費而駛往中東，加劇其他地區的船舶短缺。沙烏地阿拉伯正與客戶洽談長期合約，改走荷姆茲海峽以外的路線。接受Bloomberg訪問的石油交易員表示，他們愈來愈依據實際貨物流動、而非總統言論調整交易；由於衝突方向更難預測，也縮小押注規模。胡塞組織攻擊沙烏地阿拉伯兩座機場，造成三人死亡、數十人受傷，進一步威脅區域穩定。

收盤殖利率曲線清楚反映買盤集中之處。2年期殖利率僅下降1.05個基點至4.7577%，5年期下降3.77個基點至4.9889%。2年與10年期利差收窄4.64個基點至46.91個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄5.97個基點至84.24個基點。長債反彈強於對聯準會下一次決策最敏感的短券。

拉長比較期間，情況仍不如單日表現亮眼。10年期殖利率比一週前高1.08個基點，一個月來上升44.38個基點；30年期一週來下降0.69個基點，但一個月來仍上升35.61個基點。星期四只是部分減輕近期融資成本上升，並未完全抵銷。2年期殖利率一個月來也上升39.07個基點，說明重新定價並不限於長期財政與供給疑慮。

10年期實質殖利率當日下降4.06個基點至2.8628%，解釋了名目殖利率降幅的大部分；損益兩平通膨率下降1.63個基點至2.364%。一個月來，實質殖利率上升43.28個基點，通膨補償僅增加1.1個基點。當日能源壓力稍緩有助通膨定價，但較大的逆轉出現在長期資金的實質成本，這也是本月殖利率升幅的主要來源。

聯準會理事Waller星期四在伊斯坦堡演說，仍支持進一步緊縮，但對步調保留彈性。若數據持續符合預期，他預期需再升息，以更快將通膨帶回2%，卻不必在連續幾次會議都採取行動。下半年經濟活動增強，使他較不擔心緊縮會造成嚴重放緩；眼前更在意的是通膨多年高於目標後若再度加速，將推高消費者、投資人及訂價企業的通膨預期。

Waller也談到較長的政策期間。9月預測可能同時包含2027年初升息與稍後降息，但八位官員預期2027年底利率至少比目前高50個基點。對於主席Kevin Warsh有意停止暗示利率路徑，他為偶爾使用前瞻指引辯護，指出同僚近期表示升息不急迫，本身就已降低市場對10月升息的預期。

聖路易聯準銀行總裁Musalem在紐約一場Bloomberg活動中也表示，要及時使通膨回到目標，仍需進一步緊縮，利率應在未來六至九個月上升，但沒有明確支持本月會議升息。根據星期四美債交易報導，市場定價顯示10月升息機率約20%，並已完全反映年底前一次升息。兩人的立場都是加強緊縮，卻未要求立即連續升息。

勞動數據並未顯示解僱人數突然增加。初領失業救濟金人數降至7月以來最低；截至9月26日當週，續領人數升至171.6萬，高於市場共識的171萬及前期修正後的169.9萬。新裁員有限，與持續領取救濟金的人數增加同時存在，分別反映進入失業的人數與失業延續的情況。

其他經濟活動指標略為轉弱。8月批發庫存月增0.5%，低於預期的0.7%與前期修正後的1.4%。亞特蘭大聯準銀行第三季GDPNow成長模型估值由3.7%小降至3.6%，並非已公布的GDP結果。房貸融資則更昂貴：30年期房貸利率由7.28%升至7.4%，15年期由6.60%升至6.73%。能源方面，天然氣庫存增加850億立方英尺，高於預期的790億與前期的640億立方英尺。

殖利率處於高檔，也使部分資深投資人改變態度。Morgan Stanley Investment Management的Vishal Khanduja本週受訪表示，十年來首次看好美國債券，預期金融條件收緊終將抑制成長。他管理的$41億Eaton Vance Total Return Bond Fund截至6月已將存續期間提高至6.07年，超過基準的5.8年，這項既有配置支持了他目前的看法。他認為殖利率仍可能再上升10至15個基點，但對未來12個月相當有信心。

財政條件則對需求回升形成重要制衡。國會預算處（CBO）主任Phillip Swagel星期四在明尼阿波利斯活動中反駁僅靠加快成長就能穩定聯邦債務的主張。他表示，若利率為4%，實質經濟每年須至少成長5%；利率為5%，就須成長6%。名目成長必須持續達到7%至8%，但經濟學家預期2026年實質成長僅2.1%。

Swagel表示，CBO將在1月或2月更新預測時納入AI對成長的影響，但約占GDP 6%的結構性赤字過大，無法單靠這項改善解決。他的估算直接挑戰財政部長Scott Bessent所稱，持續超過3%的成長即可使債務比率轉向的論點。Swagel認為借款目前對利率的推升作用尚小，但警告負面衝擊可能形成循環：利息支出增加，赤字與債務擴大，融資成本再進一步上升。

## AI融資推升科技信用風險定價

新借款計畫爭奪投資人的承接能力，AI收入疑慮也加深，科技信用市場因而轉弱。ICE Data Services資料顯示，Broadcom的5年期信用違約交換（CDS）星期四擴大3個基點至紀錄高點136個基點；Oracle的違約保障成本增加約10.5個基點，收在紀錄高點261個基點。SpaceX的信用風險指標連續第二天創高。

大型融資不斷增加。Bloomberg統計，今年美國共有九筆規模至少$250億的投資等級債券發行，創歷史最多，且主要來自科技業。其AI基礎設施融資統計接近$5,000億；Goldman Sachs信用策略師採用較廣的口徑，估計全球AI相關發行超過$5,750億。兩種統計都呈現融資擴張，範圍涵蓋公司債、晶片採購與資料中心融資架構。

Allspring資深固定收益交易員Mark Clegg表示，每一項新融資公告都再占用投資人的資金，造成一年前難以想像的利差波動。T. Rowe Price投資組合經理Steven Kohlenstein則指出，即使債務分散在不同發行人、產業與結構，風險仍集中於少數公司及同一個投資週期；工具分散並未消除對AI建設的共同依賴。

目前的重新定價主要反映投資人的資金承接能力漸近飽和，而非企業現金創造能力全面崩落。許多大型借款人仍有獲利、穩定現金流與獲利成長動能，弱勢也未均勻蔓延到整個公司債市場。收盤時，美國高收益債利差小幅擴大，硬通貨新興市場債利差明顯擴大；隨長期利率下降，LQD當日報酬為0.36%，HYG下跌0.05%，EMB上漲0.20%。即使信用風險補償增加，美債上漲仍支撐了部分債券報酬。

Broadcom與OpenAI的潛在融資也有了新的規模與進度資訊。知悉初步討論的人士稱，雙方可能借款約$300億，用於採購共同開發的客製晶片，低於先前超過$500億的報導。正式程序尚未啟動，計畫仍可能改變；兩家公司均不予置評。Broadcom另已啟動一項供Anthropic受益的$600億融資，OpenAI的討論則是在其之外新增的潛在資金需求。

Oracle正另與Apollo及Goldman Sachs洽談晶片採購融資。部分市場人士設想，由外部投資人出資設立特殊目的機構，買入晶片後租給Oracle，而不是由Oracle借入無擔保債務、一次支付採購款。這種架構可能減少其他近期借款需求、緩和評等壓力，但形式仍在討論。Oracle違約保險溢價上升，反映投資人在評估替代方案時，仍不確定公司最終需承擔多少融資負擔。

騰訊考慮最快本月發行最多$50億境外債，可能包括美元與離岸人民幣。知悉洽談的人士未說明資金用途。公司6月曾募得近$47億，用於再融資及一般公司用途，包括AI開發；今年卻沒有公開債券到期，下一筆美元債到期在2028年。其流通境外債約$220億，此次提案涉及擴大融資能力，而非立即償還公開債券。

騰訊的投資支出相當可觀。AI專案與運算需求帶動截至6月季度的資本支出增加176%，達人民幣528億元，約$79億。公司一面開發模型，與中國領先業者競爭，一面經營大型雲端業務、服務其他開發商；自身能力建設與客戶運算需求，共同構成潛在融資背後的投資需求。

OpenAI的收入預期卻朝另一方向調整。知悉營運表現的人士稱，年化收入可望約為$500億，低於上月報導的近$700億。較低的收入估計拖累那斯達克100指數下跌1.39%，半導體股下跌3.39%。標普500指數跌0.47%至7,765.36，但根據Bloomberg收盤報導，成分股超過三分之二上漲，小型股大致持平。科技股下跌伴隨資金轉向民生必需品與低波動股票，而非股市全面撤退。

實際晶片需求仍強。三星公布截至9月季度的初步營業利益達107.4兆韓元，約$801億，接近去年同期的九倍，卻仍低於分析師平均預測，股價下跌2.4%。台積電季度營收增加51%。客戶提前下單，使Counterpoint將第三季DRAM價格季增預測由5%至10%調高為10%至20%。Citi分析師預期，12層HBM4價格明年將上漲100%至150%，但韓元走強使他們下修三星全年獲利預測。

當前晶片需求強勁，但更大規模的產能投資仍須有足夠報酬，才能支撐融資。Deutsche Bank策略師預期美國第三季獲利年增34%，超大型科技公司約增54%，為高利率造成的估值壓力提供重要支撐。然而隨融資成本上升，投資人對收入如何分配給晶片供應商、雲端業者與模型開發商，要求也愈來愈高。

Nvidia支持的澳洲資料中心業者Firmus Grid，在股權融資上面臨更即時的壓力。其規劃的$55億上市案未能在每股A$11的推介價格取得足夠支持，簿記結束時定價與結構仍不明朗。到了星期五亞洲早盤，知情人士稱公司預期將延後IPO，並考慮改採私募融資。這項較晚的發展，使融資困境延伸到星期四美國收盤之後。

國際清算銀行（BIS）星期四發布的論文，從政策角度檢視同一投資週期。研究員Leonardo Gambacorta與Salvatore Polizzi認為，在生產力改善降低成本前，AI可能先推高能源價格，改變潛在產出，也使產能利用率更難判斷。效率提升能否抵銷資料中心用電，部分取決於發電方式。他們並指出，若預期過度樂觀，資料中心與電網投資可能突然修正，使不確定的經濟報酬衍生金融穩定風險。

## 法國主權溢價與歐洲政策限制

最新衡量顯示，法國企業融資已大幅脫離主權殖利率曲線。Bloomberg資料指出，星期三近€2,150億高評級公司債、占流通總額38%，殖利率低於相近年期的政府公債。這一金額接近2026年初€120億的18倍，倒掛已涵蓋許多BBB級證券，不限於信用最優良的公司。

Generali Investments策略師Elisa Belgacem認為，即使法國財政困難，投資人仍信任企業基本面，整體殖利率也具吸引力。L'Oreal與TotalEnergies等跨國公司，大部分收入來自國內經濟以外。PGIM的Edward Farley對銀行較為謹慎，因其持有主權債與放款業務，與政府政策的連結更緊密，較難同樣免受財政壓力影響。

銀行股持續走弱。Stoxx 600銀行類股星期三下跌3.3%，星期四盤中又跌最多2.2%，可能創3月以來最差的兩日表現。Societe Generale已較8月高點低26%，Deutsche Bank較9月高點低18%。類股年初以來漲幅縮至12%，約為9月最高漲幅的一半。

Axiom Alternative Investments研究主管Jerome Legras將大部分波動歸因於成長、殖利率與ECB下一步的不確定性。IG的Alexandre Baradez則指出，與前次主權危機不同，法國銀行的違約保險成本低於政府；他認為這反映銀行資本更健全。市場仍擔心銀行曝險，卻未將銀行與政府信用風險作相同定價。

財政部長Roland Lescure星期四在不同場合強調，法國仍能取得融資。他告訴BBC，政府持續每兩週發債，投資人仍願意購買，只是要求更高殖利率。在倫敦政經學院，他將行情描述為全球對債務、通膨與貨幣政策預期重新定價，而非市場失靈、需要緊急干預。他也坦言公共赤字令人憂慮，必須降低。星期四盤中，法國10年期殖利率距5%不到5個基點。

ECB總裁拉加德在盧森堡與歐元區財長的非公開會議上表示，央行有工具應對威脅貨幣政策傳導、不合理且失序的市場動態，但須符合明確資格條件；她拒絕討論個別國家。這項有條件的後盾，與法國財長認為目前市場運作不需要干預的立場並存。財政可信度仍是必要條件，而基本面重新定價與政策傳導失序是不同的問題。

ECB新公布的9月會議紀錄，進一步說明長期殖利率上升的貨幣政策意義。官員認為2.5%的存款利率位於幕僚估計的中性區間，因此今年第二次升息仍是對通膨的適度回應。溝通既不應承諾預定升息序列，也不應暗示這必然是最後一次升息。

紀錄指出，有序的長端重新定價可加強政策原本希望達成的緊縮，並影響未來適當的政策利率。官員認為，近期長期殖利率變動主要來自實質期限溢價提高，與公私部門發行增加及財政不確定性有關。模型顯示，長期利率上升對成長與通膨有實質影響。薪資評估則受時點限制：薪資協商日程與傳導落差意味著，下一批有助判斷第二輪效應的資訊，大多要到明年初才會出現。

星期四多位官員都表示，目前外溢效應有限，但關注重點不同。法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin指出，能源衝擊正使財政強健與薄弱的國家都面臨金融條件收緊，卻很少見到間接通膨，亦未出現第二輪效應。荷蘭央行總裁Olaf Sleijpen也表示，持續的能源衝擊尚未使家庭通膨預期失去錨定。

首席經濟學家Philip Lane表示，目前薪資協議溫和，基礎價格未出現非線性反應。他預期明年基礎通膨會上升，但將此視為中等規模衝擊，傾向審慎、有節制的回應。斯洛維尼亞的Primoz Dolenc強調，ECB有能力避免初始價格衝擊變成持續通膨；他預期通膨到年底約為3%，若無新衝擊，未來兩年會逐步回到2%。克羅埃西亞的Ante Zigman則預期下次會議將有密集討論。這些觀點既反映目前尚無廣泛薪資與價格相互推升，也保留繼續緊縮的意願。

政府能負擔多少援助，是財政當局的另一場爭論。歐盟執委會財政主管Valdis Dombrovskis反對義大利與希臘要求更多預算彈性，但同意進一步檢視提案。現有彈性已容許符合資格的能源安全措施延續至2028年；他認為目前債市環境使財政審慎尤其重要。比利時的Vincent Van Peteghem支持暫時措施應對高能源價格，而非新增國家層級豁免條款。歐元集團主席Kyriakos Pierrakakis則強調，保護家庭與企業不能犧牲財政可信度。

英國央行總裁Andrew Bailey星期四在土耳其演說，說明了更廣泛的限制。反覆衝擊、疲弱的基礎成長與債務上升，正削弱政府緩衝下一次衰退的能力。融資成本提高推升債務比率，求助需求卻同時增加；市場若懷疑財政路徑，殖利率又可能再升。Bailey表示，第二輪通膨效應目前偏弱，但能源價格持續高檔，加上近期高通膨經驗，可能推升預期。

英國最新家庭數據顯示，壓力已傳到信用與房市。英國央行季度調查發現，信用卡違約率連續六季上升，是2008至2009年以來最長紀錄。回報違約增加與減少的貸款機構占比，淨差額達26個百分點，銀行預期第四季違約率還會上升；房貸違約率則略降，預期最後一季不變。調查期間為8月17日至9月4日，早於最近一波油價升勢，反映的是壓力較早階段的情況。

英國皇家特許測量師學會（RICS）另指出，9月新買家詢問指標下降4點至負22，是3月以來首次惡化。議定成交減少，價格下跌的情況四個月來首次更普遍。測量師已不再預期未來12個月房價會恢復上漲。平均2年期房貸利率接近6%，家庭在消費信用惡化之外，又面臨新的融資障礙。

NatWest宣布調整主權債市場中介業務，擬退出美國與歐洲一級交易商計畫，但保留英國角色。知悉計畫的人士稱，最多將裁撤十個職位，市場業務會更集中於融資、顧問與避險。另一名知情人士表示，決定與近期波動無關。此前第二季固定收益收入年減28%至£3,200萬，與該部門總收入成長形成對比。

## 亞洲標售、銀行與融資需求

日本30年期公債標售再次顯示，高絕對殖利率能吸引買家。投標倍數達3.88，前次為3.79，過去12個月平均為3.56。標售最高得標殖利率為4.12%，連續第二次超過4%，標售後債價持穩。SMBC Nikko Securities策略師Miki Den表示，高殖利率有助標售需求，但財政擴張疑慮仍使超長天期債券在次級市場較難吸引買盤。

首相高市早苗向國會提出新的政策表述，稱日本不再需要以擺脫通縮為目的的貨幣寬鬆與財政擴張，並表示尊重日本央行自主性。這與她長期以來推動再通膨的形象有所不同；然而政府仍推動食品與非酒精飲料消費稅減稅，資金來源尚有疑問。《讀賣新聞》並報導，政府考慮2026財政年度第二次追加預算。標售需求穩健之際，財政承諾與未來發債需求仍未底定。

日本企業借款也在擴大。4月至9月外幣債發行達$918億，超過一年前同期$751億的紀錄。上半年度國內發行增加10%，創¥10.6兆、約$670億新高，受SoftBank零售債與大型銀行次順位債發行帶動。

Goldman Sachs債務資本市場主管Dai Kitatani表示，境外借款換匯成日圓後可能更昂貴，但市場較深，能容納更大交易。Goldman、UBS與HSBC正擴充日本債務團隊，Nomura也成立專門的公司債部門。承銷能力增加，反映併購、AI資本支出及再融資需求；借款人願意多付部分成本，換取較大的融資規模。

南韓正考慮調整企業境外債的承銷資格。財政部向業界徵詢意見，研議限制未持有本國證券執照的投資銀行，理由是其在當地活動與完整持牌競爭者所負義務之間存在落差。今年南韓發行人境外發債增加31%至$656億，約占亞太美元與歐元發行13%。新規將影響借款人可選擇的承銷機構，實施方式仍在考慮。

殖利率上升對新加坡銀行股則較不利。星展與大華銀行各跌逾5%，華僑銀行最多跌4.8%，使海峽時報指數下跌3.5%，創2025年4月以來最大跌幅。JPMorgan分析師Harsh Wardhan Modi警告，長期殖利率升高將造成交易簿按市價評價損失，並減少資本市場活動。資產負債表成長放緩、存款競爭及財富管理手續費回歸正常，也可能導致獲利預測下修，尤其是華僑銀行。

Tiger Brokers策略師James Ooi強調，貸款收益提高是否有利，要看能否跟上銀行支付的存款及其他融資成本。銀行股長期上漲後估值偏高，使這一評估更重要。星展預估股價淨值比為2.9倍，接近歷史平均的兩倍。當日跌勢同時反映獲利重新評估與原先偏高的估值。

印度央行星期三升息後，市場繼續調整預期。Goldman Sachs、Standard Chartered、Deutsche Bank與Morgan Stanley經濟學家預期12月4日再升25個基點；部分人士預期2027年上半年再升50個基點，使利率從5.5%升至6.25%。Goldman的Santanu Sengupta預期至少再緊縮75個基點，理由包括成長具韌性、價格壓力擴散及聖嬰現象可能帶來的食品風險。

HSBC的Pranjul Bhandari對後續路徑有不同看法，預期12月升息後將長期暫停。她指出，逐步調整緊縮力道的立場，保留了任何一次會議按兵不動的彈性，並以印度央行2018年採取這一立場後、未再升息就轉向為例。Barclays與ICRA也不預期12月之後大幅緊縮。這些新預測顯示，各方對後續升息週期的幅度仍有分歧。

匯率壓力正在消耗另一項資源。Bloomberg報導，截至10月2日的四週，匯市干預是印度外匯存底減少$510億的原因之一，盧比仍接近歷史低點。Nifty 50星期四跌1.6%至2025年4月以來最低，外資今年撤出股票的金額接近$300億。高油價推升輸入性通膨、壓縮企業利潤，匯率與融資成本又加重壓力。

菲律賓債券面臨更明顯的通膨與貨幣雙重壓力。10年期殖利率星期三達7.99%，創2018年底以來最高；Bloomberg估計，伊朗戰爭開始後美元計價損失達13%，是19個新興市場中表現最差者。新的分析指出，9月美元兌披索與10年期殖利率的90日相關係數達紀錄高點0.63。Rizal Commercial Banking的Michael Ricafort提及石油、食品與匯率風險；Robeco的Philip McNicholas則表示，儘管殖利率愈來愈有吸引力，仍擔心財政立場與通膨。

中國最新刺激措施獲得不同評價。JPMorgan認為政策由國家引導、偏重供給；Citi認為重點在投資與房地產，對消費的外溢效果有限。Morgan Stanley的邢自強與Harry Zhao指出，房價下降、所得成長疲弱，持續促使家庭去槓桿。儘管先前已有穩定措施，1月至8月房地產銷售仍下降逾13%。支持基礎設施與科技的放款，可能有助達成官方4.5%至5%的成長目標，卻未解決家庭面臨的限制。

Bloomberg Economics研究員Simon Lloyd、Ana Galvao與Bjorn van Roye本週報告，也量化了高利率衝擊的成長代價。他們估計，在其他基本面不變下，光是近期利率重新定價，到2027年底就會使美國、英國與歐元區GDP減少0.2%至0.3%。到2029年底，模型估計英國與歐元區約減少0.3%，美國減少0.5%，CPI通膨同時低0.1至0.2個百分點。需求或潛在成長較強可抵銷部分效果；若衝擊由能源帶動，購買力也下降，損害就可能更大。

## 再融資壓力與分歧的通膨決策

JetBlue一筆$20億、以忠誠客戶計畫作擔保、2031年到期的債券，星期四跌至每$1面額72美分，是2024年8月發行以來最低。過去一個月利差已升破1,000個基點，公司同時面臨約$90億債務與持續現金消耗。S3 Partners估計，今年平均放空餘額占自由流通股比例為29%，高於先前的20%。

營運數字說明了燃油為何對信用如此重要。JetBlue第二季自由現金流流出$3.89億，其中營運消耗$1.55億、資本支出$2.34億。儘管收入增加14.5%，平均燃油成本仍年增76%至每加侖$4.23。Bloomberg Intelligence分析師George Ferguson表示，若燃油價格持續高檔，公司可能必須縮小規模，直到業務能穩定產生現金。當前債券損失因此對應具體營運難題，並非科技融資賣壓的一部分。

星期四Milken亞洲峰會上，私募信貸投資人指出另一種到期問題。Lord Abbett的Steve Kuppenheimer認為，2021與2022年承作的貸款尤其脆弱，因當時承作評估使用的基準利率接近零。他估計目前違約率約3%至4%，高於歷史平均2%。Apollo的Brigitte Posch提到，部分借款人的資產價值相對債務已下降；Bridgepoint的Andrew Konopelski則表示，靠出售資產還款，要看私募股權業主是否願意退出投資。

壓力並未消除放款意願。與談者指出，較高基準利率提高預期報酬，也促使承作標準與契約條款更嚴格。Posch表示，Apollo過去12個月已為約$80億亞太機會提供融資。另一方面，澳洲監管機關星期四又暫時禁止三項私募信貸產品向投資人銷售，延續對非上市市場風險的審查。

Skydance首個交易日，管理層試圖提振市場對這家總債務近$870億公司的信心。共同執行長David Ellison與Ynon Kreiz主張，與Warner Bros.合併後，降低成本可以與業務成長並進。公司仍須履行訴訟和解下的院線發行承諾。兩人星期四重申既有現金流與降債目標，並未提出新的融資協議；最新報導的總債務則界定了整合任務的規模。

巴林融資壓力集中於較短年期。2028年到期美元債殖利率達8.99%，創六年新高，比8月底高1.6個百分點。這段期間美元債下跌4.2%，伊斯蘭債券（sukuk）下跌3.5%。2028年債的利差擴大幅度高於2035年債；儘管Moody's評等比埃及高兩級，巴林殖利率仍超過埃及。

Arqaam Capital的Fady Gendy認為弱勢屬發行人個別問題；若壓力變得嚴重且持續，他預期海灣合作理事會的支持會更明確。他認為在此之前，巴林可透過私募、國內融資與伊斯蘭債券履行義務。戰爭已干擾出口、減少原油產量並損害基礎設施，Bloomberg訪調的經濟學家預期今年經濟萎縮6.6%。世界銀行估計債務超過GDP的140%，赤字為10.5%，使巴林幾乎沒有空間吸收美債殖利率上升與自身風險溢價擴大的雙重衝擊。

拉丁美洲的通膨決策則各有差異。烏拉圭在通膨連續兩個月高於4.5%目標後，將基準利率提高25個基點至6%，是2025年4月以來首次升息。9月通膨接近4.7%，仍在央行容許區間，卻遠高於3月的70年低點。官員希望避免暫時性的食品與能源漲價變成持續通膨或影響預期，仍預期在24個月政策期間內回到目標。此前自2025年7月至今年3月已連續七次降息、合計3.5個百分點，此次轉為升息。

智利9月CPI月增0.4%，低於預測的0.5%，年增率為4.1%；細項卻仍有壓力，能源上漲1.9%、運輸0.9%、食品與非酒精飲料0.6%，保險與金融服務則下降5.9%。財政部將2026年成長預測由1.8%下修至0.7%，並將2027年預測提高至3.3%。政策利率維持4.5%的決策者仍以2027年第二季通膨達3%為目標，面對疲弱活動與持續進口成本的兩難。

哥倫比亞通膨年增率由6.24%加速至6.29%，但低於調查預期的6.33%，月增0.37%。近期利率已升至12.25%，此次漲幅較小，稍微緩和立即進一步緊縮的壓力；通膨預期卻仍高於3%目標及容許區間。祕魯另公布原先待決的利率決策，因官員預期近期通膨加速只是暫時現象，意外維持利率不變。

波蘭央行總裁Adam Glapinski也降低再次升息的急迫性。他星期四表示，若價格壓力擴散且持續，準備採取行動，但目前既無第二輪效應，也沒有迫在眉睫的擔憂。他發言後，交易員降低升息預期，2年期公債殖利率下降2個基點至4.74%。Rafal Benecki帶領的ING Bank Slaski經濟學家仍預期2027年第一季升息一至兩次、每次25個基點。爭論在於燃油價格稍緩與有限外溢效應能讓央行等待多久，而非立即轉向寬鬆。

## 後續市場觀察重點

星期五紐約上午10時公布的10月密西根大學調查初值，將檢視家庭如何回應聯準會官員所擔心、可能改變預期的通膨衝擊。消費者信心預期由48.1降至47.6，預期指數由46.3降至45.9，現況指數由50.9降至50.5。Trading Economics預測通膨預期指標由4.6%升至4.7%，五年期指標由3.4%升至3.5%。相較單一信心數字，預期購買力壓力與較長期通膨信念的組合更值得關注。

波士頓聯準銀行總裁Susan Collins將於星期五紐約下午4時演說。在兩位官員最新呼籲進一步緊縮、卻對時點保留彈性之後，仍待釐清的是：目前融資成本上升是否已帶來足夠緊縮，容許再暫停一次；還是即使星期四長債需求良好，持續通膨仍要求更快的政策回應。

債市反彈也取決於美國與伊朗近期升級風險下降，能否改善實體供應。油價雖離開盤中高點，油輪安全、墨西哥灣生產中斷與運費仍是實際限制。星期五的世界農業供需預估報告（WASDE）及Baker Hughes鑽井數，將補充農業供應與能源活動的例行觀察；多國央行的不同決策都正受到食品風險與能源成本影響。

歐洲接下來的選擇，將使財政援助與通膨控制更緊密地交會。英國預算案訂於10月28日提出，家庭壓力正上升，Bailey也警告政府借款能力逐漸耗損。ECB於10月29日開會，經濟學家普遍預期暫停升息，12月再升息使存款利率達2.75%。薪資協議溫和、廣泛第二輪效應未現，有利循序調整；能源成本若持續高檔，或主權市場失序干擾政策傳導，則會分別改變評估的不同面向。

企業融資方面，下一批重要發展是大型晶片融資的條件與進度，以及騰訊可能的發債，而非又一項整體投資願景公告。Firmus預期延後IPO，也使其他資金來源能否取得成為眼前問題。潛在供給增加已使既有科技債要求更多補償；收入能否兌現、交易如何安排，以及投資人的承接能力，是下一筆融資能否順利完成的不同考驗。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Long-dated Treasuries rallied on October 8 as buyers absorbed a $22 billion 30-year auction at elevated yields, then received some relief from President Donald Trump's decision to defer further attacks on Iran until after the U.S. midterm elections. The 30-year yield fell 7.02 basis points to 5.6001%, while the 10-year declined 5.69 basis points to 5.2268%. The recovery flattened the curve and reduced both real yields and longer-term inflation compensation, although oil still finished sharply higher.

The buying was strongest at maturities where the recent selloff had made outright yields more attractive. It came without a retreat from the Federal Reserve's tightening direction: Christopher Waller argued for additional increases with flexibility over their timing, and Alberto Musalem said more restraint would be needed over the next six to nine months. Fresh labor figures continued to show limited layoffs, while higher mortgage rates illustrated the pressure already reaching borrowers.

Corporate credit presented a less uniform recovery. Technology companies' expanding financing needs drove default-insurance costs to records, even as much of the broader equity market resisted the technology selloff. In Europe, new evidence of French companies borrowing more cheaply than their government underscored the separation between international corporate earnings and sovereign fiscal risk. Central bankers were still reporting limited second-round inflation effects, but governments and vulnerable borrowers faced increasingly expensive choices.

## Long-Bond Demand Overcomes Early Energy Pressure

The Treasury auction gave the session a concrete source of long-duration demand after renewed energy concerns had pushed yields higher earlier in the day. The $22 billion sale cleared at 5.618%, close to the 5.617% when-issued yield at the 1 p.m. New York bidding deadline. Primary dealers received 6.8% of the offering, below a recent average of 10%, leaving an unusually small share for intermediaries to absorb. The previous 30-year auction had cleared at 5.308%: demand held up at a substantially higher cost to the government.

The result extended the week's successful absorption of longer debt, rather than simply carrying forward Wednesday's auction rally. Thursday brought a new sale at the longest maturity and a further daily decline in yields. Treasury subsequently repurchased $6 billion of bonds maturing in 20 to 30 years, its fourth such operation since expanding the program. The buyback added a separate purchase of outstanding long bonds after investors had taken down the new supply.

TD Securities rates strategist Molly Brooks said the demand suggested higher yields were beginning to attract buyers. She thought a rally sustained for several days could encourage investors who had been waiting for greater stability. That assessment followed a realized auction result, while its extension into broader secondary-market buying remained dependent on prices holding their gains.

Trump's social-media statement helped the rally extend. He said the U.S. would refrain from attacking Iran again before the November 3 midterms and cited productive discussions with Tehran, without giving details. That reversed the immediate expectation encouraged by an earlier Atlantic report that the White House had asked the Pentagon to prepare pre-election strike options. RBC Capital Markets strategist Izaac Brook attributed some of the relief in oil and long yields to the removal of near-term escalation risk.

Physical supply remained under pressure. Fresh attacks on tankers threatened the recent improvement in flows through the Strait of Hormuz, while Hurricane Isaias prompted producers to shut wells and evacuate personnel in the U.S. Gulf. Brent traded around $105 during the session before easing. At the fixed-income close it was $103.79 a barrel, up 3.58%, and WTI was $91.11, up 3.21%. The diplomatic comments reduced the day's extremes but left energy materially more expensive than the previous close.

Shipping conditions also pointed to a longer disruption. Supertankers were heading toward the Middle East to capture elevated freight fees, worsening vessel shortages elsewhere. Saudi Arabia was discussing longer-term contracts with customers using routes outside Hormuz. Oil traders interviewed by Bloomberg said their responses increasingly depended on physical cargo movements rather than presidential rhetoric, and that they were reducing wager sizes as the conflict's direction became less predictable. Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports, killing three people and injuring dozens, added another current threat to regional stability.

The closing Treasury curve showed where the demand concentrated. The two-year yield fell only 1.05 basis points to 4.7577%, compared with a 3.77-basis-point decline in the five-year to 4.9889%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 4.64 basis points to 46.91, and 2s30s contracted 5.97 to 84.24. Long bonds therefore recovered more strongly than securities most sensitive to the next Fed decision.

The longer comparisons remained less favorable. The 10-year yield was still 1.08 basis points above its week-earlier observation and 44.38 higher over the month. The 30-year was down 0.69 over the week but up 35.61 over the month. Thursday reduced the recent rise in borrowing costs without erasing it. The two-year's 39.07-basis-point monthly increase also showed that the repricing extended beyond long-term fiscal and supply concerns.

At 10 years, the real yield declined 4.06 basis points to 2.8628%, accounting for most of the nominal rally. Breakeven inflation fell 1.63 basis points to 2.364%. Over the month, the real yield was up 43.28 basis points and inflation compensation only 1.1. The day's energy relief helped inflation pricing, but the larger reversal was in the real cost of long-term capital, where most of the month's increase had occurred.

Waller's Thursday speech in Istanbul preserved the case for more Fed tightening while qualifying its pace. If data continued to arrive as expected, he anticipated additional increases to bring inflation back to 2% more quickly, but said those increases need not occur at consecutive meetings. Strengthening activity in the second half made him less concerned about a damaging slowdown from tighter policy. His more immediate concern was that another acceleration in inflation, after years above target, would raise expectations among consumers, investors and businesses setting prices.

The governor also drew attention to the longer policy horizon. Although the September projections could combine early-2027 increases with later cuts, eight participants expected rates to finish 2027 at least 50 basis points above their current level. He defended occasional forward guidance against Chair Kevin Warsh's intention to stop signaling the rate path, pointing out that colleagues' recent statements about a lack of urgency had themselves reduced expectations for an October increase.

Musalem supplied a separate current policy assessment at a Bloomberg event in New York. The St. Louis Fed president said further firming would be required to return inflation to target in a timely fashion and indicated that rates should rise over the next six to nine months. He stopped short of endorsing an increase at this month's meeting. By Thursday's Treasury trading account, market pricing assigned roughly a 20% chance to an October increase and fully priced a move by year-end. Both speakers supported more restraint without requiring an immediate consecutive hike.

The labor releases gave little evidence of a sudden increase in dismissals. Initial jobless claims fell to their lowest since July. Continuing claims for the week ended September 26 rose to 1.716 million, above the 1.710 million consensus and a revised 1.699 million previously. Limited new layoffs coexisted with a rise in the number remaining on benefits, distinct observations about entry into unemployment and the persistence of joblessness.

Other activity readings softened modestly. August wholesale inventories rose 0.5% month on month, below the 0.7% expectation and a revised 1.4% increase previously. The Atlanta Fed's Q3 GDPNow estimate edged down to 3.6% from 3.7%; it remained a model estimate of growth rather than a released GDP result. Mortgage borrowing became more expensive: the 30-year mortgage-rate reading increased to 7.4% from 7.28%, while the 15-year rate rose to 6.73% from 6.60%. In energy, natural-gas inventories increased 85 billion cubic feet, exceeding the expected 79 billion and the previous 64 billion build.

The high-yield environment was drawing a different response from some established investors. Morgan Stanley Investment Management's Vishal Khanduja said in an interview this week that he was constructive on U.S. debt for the first time in a decade, expecting tightening financial conditions eventually to check growth. His $4.1 billion Eaton Vance Total Return Bond Fund had already increased duration to 6.07 years as of June, above its benchmark's 5.8 years. He allowed for another 10-15 basis points of yield overshoot, while expressing strong conviction over a 12-month horizon. The June allocation was an existing position behind that current assessment, not a Thursday portfolio change.

Fiscal arithmetic supplied a substantial counterweight to the demand recovery. Congressional Budget Office Director Phillip Swagel challenged the argument that faster growth alone could stabilize federal debt. At a Minneapolis event Thursday, he said an interest-rate level of 4% would require annual real growth of at least 5%; rates of 5% would require 6%. Sustained nominal growth would need to reach 7%-8%, against economists' expectation of only 2.1% real growth for 2026.

Swagel said the CBO would incorporate AI's growth effects in upgraded projections due in January or February, but that a structural deficit of about 6% of GDP was too large for that improvement alone to resolve. His estimates directly challenged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's argument that sustained growth above 3% could bend the debt ratio. Swagel characterized borrowing's present upward influence on rates as small, while warning that a negative shock could create a feedback loop from higher interest expense to larger deficits, more debt and still higher borrowing costs.

## AI Financing Reprices Technology Credit

Technology credit weakened as new borrowing plans competed for investor capacity and questions about AI revenues sharpened. Broadcom's five-year credit-default swaps widened 3 basis points Thursday to a record 136, according to ICE Data Services. Oracle's default-protection cost increased about 10.5 basis points to a record close of 261. SpaceX's credit-risk measure reached a record for a second consecutive day.

The pressure came as large transactions multiplied. Bloomberg reported nine U.S. investment-grade offerings of at least $25 billion this year, the most on record and mostly in technology. Its tally of borrowing to fund AI infrastructure approached half a trillion dollars, while Goldman Sachs credit strategists put global AI-related issuance above $575 billion under their broader measure. The competing totals described a financing expansion reaching corporate bonds, chip purchases and data-center structures.

Allspring senior fixed-income trader Mark Clegg described each new financing announcement as another demand on investor balance sheets, bringing spread volatility that would have been difficult to imagine a year earlier. T. Rowe Price portfolio manager Steven Kohlenstein highlighted concentration in a small group of companies and the same underlying investment cycle, even when the debt appeared across different issuers, sectors and structures. Distribution across instruments was not eliminating their shared dependence on the AI buildout.

The current repricing was primarily a response to market saturation rather than a broad collapse in corporate cash generation. Many large borrowers remained profitable with steady cash flow and earnings momentum, and the weakness had not spread uniformly through the corporate market. U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly at the close, while hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. LQD returned 0.36% for the day as longer rates fell; HYG slipped 0.05% and EMB gained 0.20%. Treasury gains supported some bond returns even where credit compensation increased.

Fresh detail also revised the scale and status of Broadcom's prospective OpenAI financing. People familiar with preliminary discussions said it could involve around $30 billion of debt to purchase custom chips the companies were developing together. No formal process had begun, and the plans could change. That was smaller than the earlier report of more than $50 billion. Broadcom and OpenAI declined to comment. The new discussions added a prospective demand for capital alongside Broadcom's already launched $60 billion financing benefiting Anthropic, without converting the OpenAI proposal into an agreed transaction.

Oracle was separately talking with Apollo and Goldman Sachs about financing chip purchases. Some market participants envisaged outside investors funding a special-purpose vehicle that would buy the chips and lease them to Oracle, instead of Oracle borrowing unsecured debt to pay upfront. Such a structure could reduce other near-term borrowing needs and ease rating pressure, but its form remained under discussion. The rise in Oracle's insurance premium reflected uncertainty over the funding burden while those alternatives were being examined.

Tencent was considering as much as $5 billion of offshore bonds, potentially in dollars and offshore yuan, as early as this month. People familiar with the talks did not specify the use of proceeds. The company had raised nearly $4.7 billion in June for refinancing and general corporate purposes, including AI development, but had no public bonds maturing this year and a dollar maturity in 2028. With around $22 billion of offshore notes outstanding, the new proposal concerned an expansion of funding capacity rather than an immediate public-bond repayment.

The spending behind Tencent's funding discussion was substantial. AI projects and computing helped drive capital expenditures up 176% to 52.8 billion yuan, or $7.9 billion, in the June quarter. The company was developing models intended to compete with leading Chinese offerings while operating a large cloud business serving other developers. That combination put investment in its own capabilities and customers' computing demand behind the potential financing.

Revenue expectations moved in the opposite direction at OpenAI. People familiar with its performance said annualized revenue was on track for roughly $50 billion, against reports last month of nearly $70 billion. The lower estimate helped send the Nasdaq 100 down 1.39% and semiconductor shares down 3.39%. The S&P 500 fell 0.47% to 7,765.36, but more than two-thirds of its members advanced and small caps were little changed in Bloomberg's closing account. Technology losses coincided with rotation into staples and lower-volatility shares rather than a uniform retreat from equities.

Actual chip demand remained strong. Samsung reported preliminary September-quarter operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, or $80.1 billion, almost nine times its year-earlier level, yet fell short of the average analyst forecast; its shares lost 2.4%. TSMC's quarterly sales rose 51%. Counterpoint raised its forecast for sequential Q3 DRAM price growth to 10%-20% from 5%-10% as customers brought orders forward. Citi analysts expected prices for 12-layer HBM4 to rise 100%-150% next year, although a stronger won led them to cut Samsung's full-year profit forecast.

Those results illustrated the distinction between strong current demand and the returns needed to justify financing still larger capacity. Deutsche Bank strategists expected U.S. Q3 earnings growth of 34% year on year and roughly 54% for megacap technology companies, a substantial earnings counterweight to the valuation pressure from higher rates. Investors were nevertheless becoming more demanding about how revenue would be divided among chip suppliers, cloud providers and model developers as borrowing costs rose.

Equity financing was showing a more immediate strain at Nvidia-backed Australian data-center operator Firmus Grid. Its planned $5.5 billion listing failed to attract sufficient support at the marketed A$11 share price, and the books closed amid uncertainty over pricing and structure. By early Asian trading Friday, people familiar with the matter said the company was expected to postpone the IPO and was weighing a private funding round instead. That later development extended the financing problem beyond Thursday's completed U.S. session.

A BIS paper released Thursday offered a separate policy perspective on the same investment cycle. Researchers Leonardo Gambacorta and Salvatore Polizzi argued that AI could raise energy prices before productivity gains reduced costs, altering potential output and making capacity utilization harder to judge. Whether efficiency improvements outweighed data-center electricity use depended partly on how the power was produced. They also identified the possibility of abrupt corrections in data-center and grid investments if expectations proved too optimistic, connecting uncertain economic returns with financial stability rather than assigning a single long-run inflation outcome to the technology.

## France's Sovereign Premium and Europe's Policy Limits

New measurements showed how extensively French corporate borrowing had separated from the sovereign curve. Nearly EUR215 billion of high-grade company bonds, or 38% of the outstanding pool, traded at lower yields than government securities of similar maturity on Wednesday, according to Bloomberg. The amount was almost 18 times the EUR12 billion at the beginning of 2026. The inversion now included many BBB-rated securities, not only the highest-quality companies.

Generali Investments strategist Elisa Belgacem attributed the separation to confidence in corporate fundamentals and attractive all-in yields despite France's fiscal difficulties. Internationally exposed businesses such as L'Oreal and TotalEnergies drew much of their revenue outside the domestic economy. PGIM's Edward Farley was more cautious about banks, whose sovereign holdings and loan books created closer links to government policy. The expanded corporate-sovereign inversion did not give every French issuer the same independence from fiscal stress.

Bank equities continued to weaken. The Stoxx 600 banking sector fell as much as 2.2% Thursday after losing 3.3% Wednesday, putting it on course for its worst two-day decline since March. Societe Generale was 26% below its August peak, and Deutsche Bank 18% below its September high. The sector's year-to-date gain had shrunk to 12%, about half its September peak.

Axiom Alternative Investments research chief Jerome Legras attributed much of the volatility to uncertainty about growth, yields and the ECB's next step. IG's Alexandre Baradez pointed to a difference from the earlier sovereign crisis: French bank default-insurance costs were below the sovereign's, which he saw as evidence of stronger capitalization. Concern about banks' exposure remained, but investors were not pricing bank and government credit identically.

Finance Minister Roland Lescure used Thursday appearances to argue that France retained access to funding. He told the BBC that the government continued to issue every two weeks and that investors still wanted French bonds, albeit at higher yields. At the London School of Economics, he described a global repricing of debt, inflation and monetary-policy expectations rather than a dysfunctional market requiring emergency intervention. He also called the public deficit alarming and said it needed to be reduced. French 10-year yields were within 5 basis points of 5% during Thursday trading.

ECB President Christine Lagarde, speaking privately to euro-area finance ministers in Luxembourg, said the bank had instruments to counter unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics threatening monetary transmission, subject to clear eligibility criteria. She declined to discuss individual countries. That preserved a conditional backstop alongside the French minister's assessment that present market functioning did not warrant one. It did not remove the requirement for fiscal credibility or the distinction between fundamental repricing and disorderly transmission.

The ECB's newly published September meeting account added a more detailed monetary-policy explanation for higher longer yields. Officials had regarded a 2.5% deposit rate as within staff estimates of neutral, allowing the second increase of the year to remain a proportionate response to inflation. They wanted communication neither to promise a predetermined sequence nor to signal that the increase was necessarily the last.

The account said orderly long-end repricing could support the intended restraint and affect the appropriate future policy rate. Officials attributed recent longer-yield moves primarily to higher real term premiums, linked to greater public and private issuance and fiscal uncertainty. Their models suggested meaningful growth and inflation effects from higher long-term rates. The record also placed an important timing constraint on the wage assessment: negotiation calendars and transmission lags meant much of the next useful information on second-round effects would arrive early next year.

Thursday's speakers described limited spillovers so far, while differing in emphasis. Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said the energy shock was transmitting into tighter financial conditions across countries with both strong and weak public finances, but reported very little indirect inflation and no second-round effects. Dutch Governor Olaf Sleijpen likewise said the persistent energy shock had not unanchored household inflation expectations.

Chief Economist Philip Lane said current wage deals were moderate and that officials were not seeing a nonlinear reaction in underlying prices. He expected underlying inflation to rise next year but favored a measured response to what he characterized as a mid-sized shock. Slovenia's Primoz Dolenc emphasized the ECB's ability to prevent an initial price shock from becoming persistent inflation; he expected inflation around 3% through year-end and a gradual return toward 2% over the next two years absent new shocks. Croatia's Ante Zigman anticipated an intensive discussion at the next meeting. Their views combined a current absence of broad wage-price propagation with continued willingness to tighten.

Fiscal authorities faced a parallel argument over how much support governments could afford. European Commission finance chief Valdis Dombrovskis resisted requests from Italy and Greece for additional budget flexibility, while agreeing to examine their proposals more closely. Existing leeway already allowed qualifying energy-security measures through 2028. He argued that current bond-market conditions made fiscal prudence particularly important. Belgium's Vincent Van Peteghem favored temporary responses to high energy prices rather than new national escape clauses, while Eurogroup President Kyriakos Pierrakakis emphasized protecting households and businesses without sacrificing fiscal credibility.

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey described the wider constraint in a Thursday speech in Turkey. Repeated shocks, weak underlying growth and rising debt were reducing governments' ability to cushion another downturn. Higher borrowing costs raised debt ratios just as demands for support increased; doubts about the fiscal path could then lift yields further. Bailey said second-round inflation effects were currently subdued, but that persistence in energy prices and the recent experience of high inflation could raise expectations.

The latest British household evidence showed that those pressures were already reaching credit and housing. The BOE's quarterly survey found credit-card default rates had risen for six consecutive quarters, the longest stretch since 2008-09. The net balance of lenders reporting an increase reached 26 percentage points, and banks expected another rise in Q4. Mortgage defaults, however, fell slightly and were expected to be unchanged in the final quarter. The survey ran from August 17 to September 4, before the most recent oil escalation, so its observation concerned an earlier stage of the squeeze.

RICS separately reported that September new-buyer inquiries fell four points to minus 22, the first deterioration since March. Agreed sales declined and falling prices became more widespread for the first time in four months. Surveyors no longer expected prices to resume growth over the next 12 months. With average two-year mortgage rates approaching 6%, households faced a renewed financing obstacle alongside the consumer-credit deterioration.

NatWest announced a structural change in sovereign-market intermediation, proposing to leave U.S. and European primary-dealer programs while retaining its UK role. People familiar with the plans said as many as 10 jobs would be cut as the markets business concentrated more on financing, advisory work and hedging. A person familiar with the decision said it was unrelated to recent volatility. The withdrawal followed a 28% year-on-year fall in second-quarter fixed-income income to GBP32 million, contrasting with growth in the unit's total income.

## Asian Auctions, Banks and Funding Demand

Japan's 30-year auction provided another example of buyers responding to high outright yields. Bid-to-cover reached 3.88, compared with 3.79 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.56. The auction's high yield was 4.12%, the second consecutive offering above 4%, and bonds were steady afterward. SMBC Nikko Securities strategist Miki Den said elevated yields helped the sale, while fiscal-expansion concerns still made super-long securities harder to buy in the secondary market.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi offered a new statement about the policy regime. She told parliament that Japan no longer needed monetary easing and fiscal expansion designed to lift it out of deflation and expressed respect for BOJ autonomy. That language moved away from her longstanding association with reflation, while the government was still pursuing a food and soft-drink sales-tax reduction whose financing remained in question. It was also considering a second supplementary budget for fiscal 2026, according to Yomiuri. The auction's firm demand therefore arrived alongside unresolved fiscal commitments, not a settled reduction in supply needs.

Japanese companies were expanding borrowing on a different scale. Foreign-currency issuance reached $91.8 billion in April-September, exceeding the previous record of $75.1 billion for the corresponding period a year earlier. Domestic first-half issuance rose 10% to a record JPY10.6 trillion, or $67 billion, helped by SoftBank's retail sale and megabank subordinated debt.

Goldman Sachs debt-capital-markets head Dai Kitatani said overseas borrowing could be more expensive after swapping proceeds into yen, but deeper markets could accommodate larger transactions. Goldman, UBS and HSBC were strengthening their Japanese debt teams, while Nomura created a specialist corporate-bond unit. The expansion in underwriting capacity reflected M&A and AI capital demands as well as refinancing, with borrowers accepting some extra cost to obtain scale.

South Korea was considering a change to who could arrange its companies' overseas bonds. The finance ministry sought industry feedback on restrictions for investment banks without domestic securities licenses, citing gaps between their local activity and the obligations of fully licensed competitors. Offshore sales by Korean issuers were up 31% this year to $65.6 billion. The proposed rules would affect access to arrangers in a market supplying about 13% of Asia-Pacific dollar and euro issuance; implementation remained under consideration.

Higher yields were less welcome in Singapore's banking shares. DBS and United Overseas Bank fell more than 5% each, and OCBC dropped as much as 4.8%, pulling the Straits Times Index down 3.5%, its worst loss since April 2025. JPMorgan analyst Harsh Wardhan Modi warned that rising long yields would produce trading-book mark-to-market losses and reduce capital-markets activity. Slower balance-sheet growth, deposit competition and normalization of wealth-management fees could also prompt earnings downgrades, particularly at OCBC.

Tiger Brokers strategist James Ooi emphasized the relationship between asset yields and funding costs: higher loan returns would help only if they kept pace with what banks paid for deposits and other finance. Elevated valuations made that assessment more consequential after the sector's long rally. DBS traded at 2.9 times forward book value, almost twice its historical average. The day's declines thus combined an earnings reassessment with a costly starting valuation, rather than a simple assumption that higher rates invariably benefit lenders.

India's adjustment continued after the RBI's Wednesday increase. Economists at Goldman Sachs, Standard Chartered, Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley expected another 25-basis-point move on December 4; some envisaged a further 50 basis points in H1 2027, taking the rate from 5.5% to 6.25%. Goldman's Santanu Sengupta expected at least 75 basis points of additional tightening, citing resilient growth, broader price pressure and prospective El Nino food risks.

HSBC's Pranjul Bhandari disagreed on the subsequent path, expecting a December increase followed by a prolonged pause. She argued that calibrated tightening preserved the ability to hold at any meeting, recalling the RBI's 2018 adoption of that stance without further increases before it reversed course. Barclays and ICRA also did not expect sharp tightening beyond December. The new forecasts revealed disagreement over the extent of the cycle, not just endorsement of the increase already delivered.

Currency pressure was consuming another resource. Bloomberg reported that intervention contributed to a $51 billion decline in India's foreign-exchange reserves in the four weeks through October 2, while the rupee remained close to its record low. The Nifty 50 fell 1.6% Thursday to its lowest since April 2025, and foreign equity withdrawals approached $30 billion for the year. Elevated oil costs weighed on imported inflation and corporate margins as the currency and financing costs intensified the strain.

Philippine debt faced a more pronounced combination of inflation and currency weakness. The 10-year yield had reached 7.99% Wednesday, its highest since late 2018, and Bloomberg calculated dollar losses of 13% since the Iran war began, the weakest performance among 19 emerging markets. A new analysis put the September 90-day correlation between dollar-peso and the 10-year yield at a record 0.63. Michael Ricafort of Rizal Commercial Banking cited oil, food and currency risks, while Robeco's Philip McNicholas remained concerned about the fiscal stance and inflation despite increasingly attractive yields.

China's latest stimulus drew a contrasting assessment. JPMorgan characterized the package as state-guided and supply-heavy, while Citi saw limited consumption spillover from its focus on investment and property. Morgan Stanley's Robin Xing and Harry Zhao argued that falling home values and weak income growth continued to encourage household deleveraging. Property sales fell more than 13% in January-August, despite earlier stabilization efforts. Lending support for infrastructure and technology could help deliver the official 4.5%-5% growth objective without resolving those household constraints.

The higher-rate shock also had a quantified, conditional growth cost. Bloomberg Economics researchers Simon Lloyd, Ana Galvao and Bjorn van Roye estimated in a note this week that recent rate repricing alone would reduce U.S., UK and euro-area GDP by 0.2%-0.3% by end-2027, holding other fundamentals fixed. By end-2029 the modeled reduction reached about 0.3% in the UK and euro area and 0.5% in the U.S., alongside CPI inflation 0.1-0.2 percentage point lower. Stronger demand or potential growth could offset part of that effect; an energy-driven shock could enlarge it by also reducing purchasing power.

## Refinancing Stress and Divergent Inflation Decisions

JetBlue's $2 billion loyalty-program-backed bond due in 2031 fell to 72 cents on the dollar Thursday, its lowest since issuance in August 2024. Its spread had moved above 1,000 basis points over the past month as the airline struggled with roughly $9 billion of debt and continuing cash consumption. S3 Partners put average short interest at 29% of float this year, up from 20%.

The operating figures explained why fuel mattered so much to the credit. JetBlue used $389 million of free cash flow in Q2, including $155 million for operations and $234 million of capital expenditure. Average fuel costs rose 76% year on year to $4.23 a gallon despite a 14.5% increase in revenue. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst George Ferguson said sustained high fuel prices could require the airline to shrink toward a business capable of generating cash regularly. That assessment put the current bond losses beside a specific operating challenge rather than treating them as part of the technology financing selloff.

Private-credit investors identified a different maturity problem at Thursday's Milken Asia Summit. Lord Abbett's Steve Kuppenheimer said loans originated in 2021 and 2022 were especially vulnerable because they were underwritten near zero base rates. He put current defaults around 3%-4%, above a historical average of 2%. Apollo's Brigitte Posch pointed to borrowers whose asset values had fallen relative to debt, while Bridgepoint's Andrew Konopelski said repayment through asset sales depended on private-equity owners' willingness to exit.

The pressure had not eliminated lending appetite. Higher base rates were raising prospective returns and encouraging tighter underwriting and covenants, panelists said. Posch said Apollo had financed about $8 billion of Asia-Pacific opportunities in the previous 12 months. Australia's regulator, meanwhile, temporarily prohibited three more private-credit products from being offered to investors Thursday, extending its scrutiny of risks in unlisted markets.

Skydance's first trading day brought a management effort to build confidence in a borrower carrying nearly $87 billion of total debt. Co-chief executives David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz argued that growth could accompany cost reduction after the Warner Bros. combination. The company still faced theatrical-release commitments under its lawsuit settlement. Their Thursday presentation reiterated existing cash-flow and debt-reduction targets rather than adding a new financing agreement, while the newly reported debt total defined the scale of the integration task.

Bahrain's financing strain was concentrated at shorter maturities. Its dollar bonds due in 2028 yielded 8.99%, a six-year high and 1.6 percentage points above late-August levels. Dollar debt had lost 4.2% over that interval and sukuk 3.5%. The 2028 spread widened more than the 2035 issue, and Bahrain's yields exceeded Egypt's despite a Moody's rating two notches higher.

Arqaam Capital's Fady Gendy described the weakness as issuer-specific and expected Gulf Cooperation Council support to become more explicit if it turned large and sustained. He thought Bahrain could meanwhile meet obligations through private placements, domestic funding and sukuk. The war had disrupted exports, reduced crude output and damaged infrastructure; economists surveyed by Bloomberg expected a 6.6% contraction this year. With a World Bank estimate of debt above 140% of GDP and a deficit of 10.5%, the borrower had little room to absorb the combination of higher Treasury yields and its own risk premium. Regional assistance remained an investor expectation conditional on worsening stress.

Latin American inflation decisions were more differentiated. Uruguay raised its benchmark 25 basis points to 6%, its first increase since April 2025, after two months of inflation above the 4.5% target. September inflation was nearly 4.7%, within the bank's tolerance band but well above March's 70-year low. Officials intended to prevent temporary food and energy increases from becoming persistent or affecting expectations, and still expected convergence to target within their 24-month horizon. The move reversed direction after seven cuts totaling 3.5 percentage points between July 2025 and March.

Chile's September CPI rose 0.4% month on month, below the 0.5% forecast, with annual inflation at 4.1%. The detail remained less comfortable: energy rose 1.9%, transport 0.9% and food and nonalcoholic beverages 0.6%, while insurance and financial services fell 5.9%. The finance ministry had cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.7% from 1.8% and raised the 2027 estimate to 3.3%. Policymakers, holding rates at 4.5%, continued to aim for 3% inflation by Q2 2027, confronting weak activity alongside persistent imported costs.

Colombia's annual inflation accelerated to 6.29% from 6.24%, but less than the 6.33% survey expectation; prices rose 0.37% on the month. That smaller increase eased some immediate pressure for additional tightening after the recent rise to 12.25%, while expectations remained above the 3% target and its tolerance band. Peru, in a separate resolution of its pending decision, unexpectedly held borrowing costs because officials expected the recent inflation acceleration to be temporary.

Poland's governor similarly reduced the urgency of another increase. Adam Glapinski said Thursday that he was ready to act if price pressure spread and became persistent, but saw neither second-round effects nor an imminent reason for concern. Traders pared hike expectations after his remarks, and the two-year government yield fell 2 basis points to 4.74%. ING Bank Slaski economists led by Rafal Benecki still expected one or two quarter-point moves in Q1 2027. The debate concerned how long fuel-price relief and limited spillovers would permit patience, not an immediate shift toward easing.

## Forward Market Significance

Friday's preliminary October Michigan survey, due at 10 a.m. New York time, will provide the next household test of an inflation shock that Fed officials say could alter expectations. Sentiment is expected at 47.6 after 48.1, with consumer expectations at 45.9 after 46.3 and current conditions at 50.5 after 50.9. Trading Economics forecasts put the inflation-expectations measure at 4.7% after 4.6% and the five-year measure at 3.5% after 3.4%. The combination of expected purchasing-power pressure and longer-horizon inflation beliefs will matter more than a sentiment headline alone.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins speaks Friday at 4 p.m. New York time. Her assessment follows two fresh calls for further tightening that left the timing flexible. The remaining question is whether officials see the current rise in borrowing costs as sufficient restraint to allow another pause, or whether persistent inflation warrants a faster policy response despite Thursday's long-bond demand.

The rally also depends on whether the reduction in near-term U.S.-Iran escalation risk improves physical supply. Tanker security, Gulf production interruptions and freight costs remain operative constraints after oil's retreat from its intraday peak. Friday's WASDE release and Baker Hughes rig counts add scheduled observations on agricultural supply and energy activity. They arrive while food risks and energy costs are influencing several distinct central-bank decisions.

Europe's next choices bring fiscal support and inflation control into close proximity. The UK budget is scheduled for October 28, with household strain increasing and Bailey warning that borrowing capacity is being depleted. The ECB meets October 29; economists broadly expect a pause followed by a December increase that would take the deposit rate to 2.75%. Moderate wage agreements and the absence of broad second-round effects favor a measured pace, while sustained energy costs or disorderly sovereign-market transmission would change different parts of that assessment.

For corporate funding, the next material developments are the terms and progress of the large chip financings and Tencent's possible bond sale, rather than another announcement of aggregate investment ambitions. Firmus's expected IPO postponement adds an immediate question about alternative capital access. Existing technology debt is already demanding more compensation as prospective supply grows, leaving revenue delivery, transaction structure and investor capacity as separate tests of how smoothly the next financing can clear.

overall_summary.headline: Strong auction demand lifts long Treasuries as deferred Iran attacks ease escalation risk
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Buyers absorbed the $22 billion 30-year Treasury auction at 5.618%, with primary dealers taking just 6.8% of the sale against a recent 10% average. Treasury's subsequent $6 billion long-bond buyback added demand. The rally extended after Trump said further attacks on Iran would wait until after the November 3 midterms, easing near-term escalation risk.

The 30-year yield fell 7.02 basis points to 5.6001%, and the 10-year fell 5.69 basis points to 5.2268%, outpacing the two-year's 1.05-basis-point decline. The 2s10s curve narrowed 4.64 basis points to 46.91. A 4.06-basis-point fall in the 10-year real yield to 2.8628% accounted for most of the nominal rally; breakeven inflation declined 1.63 basis points to 2.364%. The recovery only partly reversed the recent repricing: the 10-year yield remained 44.38 basis points higher over the month.

Brent still closed up 3.58% at $103.79 as tanker attacks and Gulf production interruptions constrained supply. Waller and Musalem supported further Fed tightening without insisting on an immediate increase, while limited layoffs offered little evidence of a sudden labor downturn.

Credit did not share a uniform recovery. Broadcom and Oracle default-protection costs reached records as prospective chip financings competed for investor capacity and OpenAI revenue expectations weakened. U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly and hard-currency EM spreads noticeably. In France, nearly EUR215 billion of high-grade corporate bonds traded below comparable sovereign yields in Wednesday's measurement, highlighting the separation between international corporate earnings and fiscal risk. The ECB retained a conditional backstop while reporting limited second-round inflation effects. Friday's Michigan survey will test whether the energy shock is lifting household inflation expectations.
